subject: Pegasus private cluster — hotpath stalls and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Linda Vo <linda.vo@pegasus-health.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@pegasus-health.com
Date: 2026-12-05T08:14:22-08:00
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 stalls on private cluster (Pegasus)

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

We started seeing sustained p95 and p99 token latencies spike on our private deployment in us-west-2 this morning around 07:40 PST. Errors are mostly 502/504s from the model nodes, and a subset of long-running requests stall in the hotpath (inference timeouts after 45s). Throughput has dipped ~28% despite normal request volume.

We've attached a perf dump and service profile from the last hour (perf_dump_pegasus_20261205.tar.gz, svc_profile_pegasus.csv). Early notes from our ops team: IO queue depth to the NVMe cache spiked, and a few nodes show elevated CPU sys time while GPU utilization remained steady.

This is impacting live triage; can Redwood open an urgent remediation lane? We need a short mitigation plan (next 2 hours) and an ETA for a root-cause patch. Looping Chris (infra) and ops for visibility.

Thanks,
Linda Vo
Head of Platform Reliability
Pegasus Health

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Linda Vo <linda.vo@pegasus-health.com>, Chris Patel <chris.patel@pegasus-health.com>, ops@pegasus-health.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-05T08:37:10-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 stalls on private cluster (Pegasus)

Hi Linda / Chris — thank you for the logs, this is top priority. Quick summary of what we see so far from the dump you sent: a) NVMe read tail latency spikes coincide with a KV-cache miss storm on hotshard IDs, b) kernel-level context switching spikes on the host indicating IO contention, c) several model processes hit fallback codepath that increases CPU pre- and post-processing overhead.

Immediate mitigations we are recommending for the next 60–90 minutes (can be done without code change):
- Route new traffic for latency-sensitive routes to the warm pool for Pegasus in us-west-2 (we can shift 30% traffic now).
- Temporarily increase per-node IO queue limits and raise host-level aio_max_requests to alleviate NVMe queues.
- Disable aggressive prefix prefetch on the affected model variant to reduce KV cache churn (config flip).
- If necessary, scale the cluster by +1 GPU node to give headroom for draining hotshards.

I'll coordinate the changes with your ops team if you approve. We will also enable detailed kernel tracing and collect another short perf dump for the engineering team to analyze.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Office: +1 415-555-0192

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Linda Vo <linda.vo@pegasus-health.com>, Chris Patel <chris.patel@pegasus-health.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T11:05:02-08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Pegasus hotpath stall — urgent remediation + exec sync

Team — following the customer report and our mitigations in-flight, we have partial relief after routing 35% of traffic to the warm pool and raising aio_max_requests. However the root cause looks like coordinated KV-cache churn on a small set of shards that causes repeated NVMe IO spikes and then model fallback to a CPU-heavy codepath (kernel selection hitting a non-optimal path when GPU queue stalls). We should consider both an operational short-term patch and a targeted runtime fix.

Priority asks (please action in order):
1) Jonas: cut a narrow runtime hotfix branch to prevent fallback path from running when NVMe latency exceeds X ms — instead spike-backoff the request rate and surface an explicit 429 to caller. This avoids long-running stalls and reduces p99 tail.
2) Karthik: prepare a quant-aware kernel update candidate (small sched tweak) that reduces thread context switches during IO stalls; include perf test plan.
3) Marissa & Laura: prepare an exec one-pager for Pegasus leadership (CTO and Head of Ops) summarizing impact, mitigations applied, and ETA for hotfix and kernel candidate. Target: 90-minute exec note + 4-hour remediation timeline.

Customer impact: ~28% throughput reduction, p99 up 4.8x, error rate elevated primarily from timeouts. We must avoid broad rollout until we've validated the hotfix in a staging mirror of Pegasus config.

I'll take point on the postmortem and follow-up runbook. If anything looks risky to deploy to their private cluster, call it out — we will seek exec approval for emergency change.

Soojin

From: Linda Vo <linda.vo@pegasus-health.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Chris Patel <chris.patel@pegasus-health.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T17:02:10-08:00
Subject: Re: Pegasus private cluster — hotpath stalls and mitigation plan

Thanks everyone — the temporary routing and IO parameter changes reduced the p99 tail and cleared most of the 504s. Throughput is back to ~93% of baseline. Our ops folks saw the NVMe queue spikes stop after the aio_max_requests tweak.

Pegasus leadership wants a short post-incident brief and the proposed hard fix cadence before they commit to a broader on-prem patch window. Linda (our CTO) asked for:
- 1-page timeline for the hotfix and kernel candidate (by EOD PST)
- A verification plan for a staged rollout to their private cluster
- Confirmation that the hotfix will not cause increased 5xxs for other customers in the same private control plane

We appreciate the fast triage. Please send the one-pager and verification plan and we'll schedule a follow-up call with Pegasus execs tomorrow morning.

Regards,
Linda Vo
Head of Platform Reliability
Pegasus Health
